claims.evidence_quote: Ten vanilla samples native to Madagascar, Mexico, French Polynesia, Papua New Guinea, and La Réunion were collected.
claims.claim: Ten purchased sample entries: Madagascar 4, Réunion 2, Mexico 1 (all planifolia); French Polynesia 2, PNG 1 (all tahitensis), seven versus three.
claims.boundary: Counts derived from Table 5; not ten countries, independent farms, harvest years, or a representative fraud survey.

claims.evidence_quote: Glass tube (syrup sugar, pods 300 g/L, vanilla seeds)
claims.claim: MAD3 is described with syrup sugar, pods 300 g/L and vanilla seeds, unlike a simple dry-pod entry.
claims.boundary: Report matrix heterogeneity; do not assert measured syrup effects or label it fraudulent.

claims.evidence_quote: For every 15 g of vanilla sample, 100 mL of solvent was used. The extraction was performed at ambient temperature and lasted for 72 h with continuous stirring.
claims.claim: Laboratory maceration used 50:50 water/ethanol, 15 g/100 mL, 72 h; followed by SPE and compound-specific analysis.
claims.boundary: Not a validation across finished foods or every retail powder/paste matrix.

claims.claim: Vanillin relative abundance in the measured VOC profile varied from 35.1% to 81.9%.
claims.boundary: Not vanillin percentage by bean weight, purity, extraction yield or sensory potency. Main text calls mean 66.1% concentration; retain relative-abundance interpretation.

claims.evidence_quote: While the plot shows a clear separation of vanilla pods by species, differentiation based on geographic origin is less pronounced.
claims.claim: VOC PCA differentiated species in the observed set more clearly than geography.
claims.boundary: Exploratory fit, not out-of-sample accuracy; do not convert plot separation into sensitivity/specificity.

claims.evidence_quote: δ13C values of vanillin of V. planifolia range from −20.5‰ to −19.1‰
claims.claim: Seven planifolia entries had vanillin δ13C −20.5 to −19.1‰; Table 4 tahitensis entries −16.7 to −16.4‰.
claims.boundary: Observed ranges in 10 entries only, not universal species thresholds or certified origin intervals.

claims.evidence_quote: the sample from Mexico can be found in the same group as the ones from Madagascar
claims.claim: Combined VOC/isotope PCA grouped Mexico with Madagascar; Réunion and Madagascar also cluster together.
claims.boundary: Authors suggest climate explanations, not proven geographic causation or measured growing conditions.

claims.evidence_quote: In the present study, statistical analyses were conducted using R (version 4.4.0) to differentiate vanilla extracts from various regions and species.
claims.claim: Statistics section supplies software only. Main text reports t-tests/PCA, not a trained classifier evaluated on independent specimens.
claims.boundary: No described held-out set, cross-validation, group splits, confusion matrix, classifier accuracy or external cohort. This is absent reporting, not proof of hidden misconduct.

claims.evidence_quote: The ten in-house vanilla extract samples were analyzed with the PRM experiment and none showed the presence of the glycosylated precursor of ethyl vanillin.
claims.claim: No ethyl vanillin glucoside detected in ten in-house extracts; PRM used to distinguish isomeric peaks.
claims.boundary: No universal absence proof; main-text precursor result lacks numerical LOD/LOQ/recovery supporting a universal threshold.

claims.evidence_quote: Ethyl vanillin was absent in all analyzed vanilla extracts.
claims.claim: No ethyl vanillin detected in the analyzed extracts.
claims.boundary: Detection in a purported bean-only extract merits investigation; does not make all ethyl-vanillin-containing products fraudulent. No market prevalence estimate.

claims.evidence_quote: the δ13C value of ethyl vanillin was stable within the uncertainty range of ±0.2‰ between 5 mg/L and 144 mg/L.
claims.claim: Ethyl-vanillin spike experiment reported a stable carbon isotope interval 5–144 mg/L, ±0.2‰.
claims.boundary: Concentration in the analytical experiment, not a food legal limit, universal LOD or universal authenticity cutoff.

claims.evidence_quote: at concentrations below 21 mg/L, δ2H values of ethyl vanillin could not be accurately determined.
claims.claim: Ethyl-vanillin hydrogen result concentration-sensitive below 21 mg/L; ≥72 mg/L synchronized trends suggest possible memory effects.
claims.boundary: Conclusion summarizes 21–72 mg/L, but discussion flags 72 and above. Do not claim an unqualified safe upper boundary.

claims.evidence_quote: when properly separated, the presence of ethyl vanillin does not interfere with vanillin’s isotope ratios.
claims.claim: Authors conclude adequate chromatographic separation permits vanillin isotope measurement despite added ethyl vanillin.
claims.boundary: Not a study of added non-bean vanillin, not proof normal vanillin isotope ratio excludes ethyl vanillin, not non-interference at every concentration.

claims.evidence_quote: performing 15 runs of standard solution in a single sequence
claims.claim: Within-run precision used 15 runs of a standard solution.
claims.boundary: Technical repetition, not 15 independent origin samples; analytical precision is not classification validation.

claims.evidence_quote: These three molecules were selected due to their relatively high abundance, and they fall into a region without overlapping with other compounds.
claims.claim: Homovanillic acid, 4-ethoxymethyl-phenol and vanillyl alcohol selected as potential minor markers based on abundance/separation.
claims.boundary: Potential markers characterized in this same small set, not independently validated origin fingerprints; label-aware feature-selection leakage cannot be established from reported methods.

claims.evidence_quote: mimic the δ13C value of the natural vanillin by mixing synthetic/biosynthetic vanillin and ex-glucose vanillin
claims.claim: Authors review carbon-isotope overlap/mimicry as rationale for complementary hydrogen and other measurements.
claims.boundary: Cited background, not a blending result generated by these ten samples; underlying cited studies not independently retrieved.

claims.evidence_quote: Further studies based on analyzing more samples from different sources and origins are needed to confirm and refine these preliminary findings.
claims.claim: Authors explicitly regard these as preliminary and request wider sampling.
claims.boundary: Supports research interpretation, not blanket origin guarantees.
